Start with sqlite3 here http://zetcode.com/db/sqlite/.

Once you've made your own database, run some queries against it see if you can get the data you need, this is simply a select statement. For instance, make a books table, add some data to it, then run select * from books; to get all of your books.

Once you feel comfortable with selecting data from columns, move on to joins. Add an author table with foreign keys etc, relate the books and authors tables together, use select statements with joins to get the authors of books. Take a look at schema design to get an idea of how tables look.

All of the above should be accomplisable within 2 weeks. Hell, with dedication you could have it done in a day.

This is what you should be able to answer. - what is a relational database? - what's the difference between foreign keys and primary keys? What's the most common primary key? - can I build my own schema? - what's the difference between a one-to-one, one-to-many and many-to-many relationship and how would I draw them as a schema? - how to I select specific data from a table I created? - how do I select data that exists on a table that's related to the table I'm querying? - if I'm given this question, "we want a database for a drama movie, this movie will have characters, secret children of characters and people who kidnap characters. How should I design my database to map all of these out in the most efficient way?"

If you can map out that last schema effectively, you should be pretty well on your way to understanding sql databases. You should also be able to navigate to any piece of data from any starting point on that table and be able to explain the best query to get the data you desire.

Good luck!

Have you ever been forced into something you didn't want to do by a medical professional? What happened?

Natural childbirth. I don't know if the admitting nurse in the maternity ward was having a bad day or just didn't feel like working, but she sent me home with a "take a Tylenol, relax and we'll see what happens" delivered in a patronizing tone. I had been in early labor since 6 am and was moving into active labor by 7 pm. This wasn't my first rodeo. I knew exactly what was happening with my body. I told her I would see her later. So, I took the damned Tylenol and a bath writhing in pain the entire time. After the bath, I just laid on my bed wrapped in a towel too tired to dress. Another contraction hit, I felt a pop and a gush. It was time to go back to the hospital. Saw the same bitch nurse. When I told her my water broke she asked if maybe I hadn't peed myself a little. If I hadn't been in so much pain, I would have happily clawed her eyes out. She kept me waiting in that observation room for nearly an hour before finally giving the go ahead to admit me to a delivery room. I was still waiting for my epidural and the nurse's assistant was still setting up the room with all the tools the doctor might need when my body started pushing. It was the strangest thing it's ever done. There was no thought behind it. It just started happening. I had to concentrate and fight to not push. I knew my doctor had only been called about 30 minutes ago and was likely still on the way. I started crying at this point because I knew it was too late for drugs. After that contraction passed, I told the setup gal I needed to push. She got this panicked look on her face, told me not to, and called for my favorite nurse in the whole wide world. When she decided to show up I told her the same thing I told the other girl, and she confirmed what I already knew (my doctor wasn't at the hospital yet) and also told me not to push. I fought myself for the next 5 agonizing minutes before my doctor swept into the room. I swear I heard angels singing when I saw his kind, smiling face. I told him what I'd told everyone else and he said, "well, when you feel the need to push, the answer is usually to push." He checked me to make sure I was fully dialated and gave me the green light to start pushing. About 10 minutes later my 2nd son was born. And you know what? Even though it wasn't what I had planned or wanted, I wouldn't change it. The experience was incredible. More than anything anyone had ever described about natural childbirth.

This is probably a highly typical experience that doesn't need elaboration for most of you but whatever, I'm going to anyway. My middle-class parents were forward thinking enough to send me to the dentist early in life to have orthodontic work done to straighten my teeth and ensure that they would be healthy for as long as possible. As a child this was the worst. The procedures were painful and the apparatus I had to wear in the meantime (mouthpieces, braces) were also painful, almost worse in their constant aching way, at least the procedures were done in a few hours...I was also a particularly rude child to my dentist, I would scream at him and complain about the pain and throw every curse word I could at him and he just took it. I was the reason Dentists have such a high suicide rate. Coincidentally I later learned from my sisters that my mother was outside the room able to hear all the terrible things I said but decided not to punish me for them. Perhaps if she had, I would have been a little easier on the guy but she let me let loose on him.

Fast forward 15 years later and I'm a young adult with nice, straight teeth that are healthy and look decent when I smile. I could not appreciate it more when I see some of my peers who are my age who have mouthes full of crooked terrible looking teeth. Some of them never smile with their teeth showing. It makes me feel like a piece of shit that my parents were good enough to me to do that for me and I didn't appreciate what they were doing one bit until later. It breaks my heart that my Dentist suffered all that abuse that I dished out to him and now that I'm finally able to appreciate his work and everything has come to fruition, he's retired and I can't explain to him how glad I am that I went through all of it and how much I truly appreciate him. It makes it worse that last I saw him he looked about 20 years older than his actual age, probably due to the stress of dealing with patients like me.

Dentists/Orthodontists/Dental Hygenists or whatever, if you're reading this, if you work with bratty kids who spit on you and curse at you for the pain you cause them, take it from me that someday they will appreciate what you've done for them. It IS all worth it in the end. I would absolutely submit my own children to the same fate knowing full well the pain it would cause them and the benefit it would give later on in life. Oh yeah and thanks Dr. Mason, your work is well done and I truly don't deserve to have such a nice set of teeth.
